prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Dallas after a truck accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — and I recommend calling a handful of firms that handle serious truck-accident cases and have the resources to investigate (accident reconstruction, experts, trial experience). Below are a few firms with strong reputations for trucking and catastrophic-injury work in Texas and Dallas-area cases, plus why you should call them. (If you want, tell me your Dallas ZIP and a few facts about the crash and injuries and I’ll pull a tailored list with phone numbers and a short script to use.)

Firms to call and why
- Morgan & Morgan (handles truck collisions nationwide, including Texas)
  - Why: very large firm with experience on complex trucking matters, resources for experts and reconstruction, contingency-fee representation, and experience negotiating with big insurer defense teams.
- Nix Patterson (Nix Patterson LLP or similarly named successor firms)
  - Why: Texas-based plaintiffs’ firm known for high-stakes catastrophic-injury and wrongful-death litigation, trial experience, and handling large commercial-defendant cases.
- Clark, Love & Hutson, LLP
  - Why: Texas personal-injury trial firm with an established Dallas presence and experience with commercial vehicle and trucking cases.
- Bailey & Galyen (Bailey & Galyen, P.C.)
  - Why: Texas regional firm that handles trucking and catastrophic injury cases, with trial experience and local know-how for dealing with Texas courts and insurers.
- The Law Offices of Jim Adler (“The Texas Hammer”) — or other long-standing Texas plaintiff firms
  - Why: well-known Texas plaintiff firms often have local teams, advertising presence, and experience handling serious personal-injury matters involving trucks.

Why these types of firms
- Trucking cases can involve complex liability issues (driver logs, maintenance records, cargo/Hz regulations, company policies, CSA scores, black boxes). Larger or specialty plaintiff firms typically have the budget and relationships with accident-reconstruction experts, medical experts, and investigators needed to develop the case.
- You want a firm that will (a) investigate quickly while evidence is fresh, (b) have trial experience if insurer offers are low, and (c) handle communications with insurers and the trucking company so you can focus on recovery.

How to choose among firms (questions to ask on the first call)
- Do you handle commercial vehicle/truck accidents regularly? Ask for a case or verdict example.
- Who will handle my case day to day — a partner, senior associate, or paralegal?
- Do you have experience trying truck-accident cases in Dallas county courts?
- Will you advance out-of-pocket costs for experts and investigations?
- What is your fee structure and do you offer a free consultation?
- Can you provide client references or online reviews?

What to have ready when you call
- Date/time/location of crash, police report number (if available)
- Photos, videos, and contact info for witnesses
- Names of the trucking company and insurance info (if you have it)
- Medical treatment info/treatment providers and hospital records
- Your preferred contact phone/email

If you’d like, tell me:
- the Dallas ZIP where you live or where the crash occurred,
- a brief summary of injuries,
- whether the police report identified the truck driver as at fault,

and I’ll prepare a short, verified list of 4–6 Dallas-area attorneys (with phone numbers and a two-sentence reason to call each) and a short script you can use on the initial call.
